purpose: Read-only incident analysis and proposed design; no engine correction or run intervention. Reproductions inject tiny deterministic failures and never probe browser capacity.
conclusion: Confirmed composition defects between admission, allocation error contracts and recovery. No single physical memory cause or global leak has been proved.

findings.title: Concurrent recovery pressure deadlocks SIFT admission
findings.mechanism: Pressure survives through useful retry. Each retry requests ArrayBuffer admission. blockingPressure treats another queued pressured operation as a producer and returns before canWaitForMemory; mutual dependencies never reach no-independent-producer handling.
findings.consequence: Eight recovery pressures and ten queued SIFT operations remain with no active execution. Five-error guard cannot advance because no retry runs.

findings.title: RGB window wrapper discards allocator cause and misclassifies arbitrary RangeError
findings.mechanism: readWindow catches output allocation, row allocation and nested storage RangeError together and replaces them with MEMORY_ALLOCATION without cause, allocationKind or requestedBytes. Genuine allocation refusal and bounds error become indistinguishable.
findings.consequence: The recovery path loses domain-aware reclamation and causal wait. Its missing requested extent falls back to 1 MiB. The test shows five identical retries and no call to typed reclaim for both injected error types.
findings.limit: Actual native cause of the PatchMatch failure cannot be reconstructed from its rewritten error.

findings.title: Allocator ownership and pressure admission are incompletely connected
findings.mechanism: RGB scratch/window and Elastic input/output have policy reservations without full backing records; Elastic memory admission declares no domains. SIFT readRect allocates before registration and does not annotate failed extent.
findings.consequence: Diagnostics are known owners only. Some paths can grow during pressure while others are blocked. A policy allowance and backing retirement are not proof of a successful new allocation.

findings.title: PatchMatch partial texture and in-flight fields lack sufficiently fine checkpoints
findings.mechanism: Texture mask is published only after all tiles; failure disposes the partial mask. The outer dense image finally aborts other in-flight fields. Existing checkpoints keep validated products, not arbitrary native iteration fronts.
findings.consequence: A resumable detector does not imply preservation of every partial internal result.

findings.title: Failure telemetry and terminal settlement miss structural stalls
findings.mechanism: Elastic recovery callbacks only update local metrics, losing public reclaim/wait episodes. Automatic session awaits active provider promises; no structural stall transition exists for a closed waiting cycle.
findings.consequence: PatchMatch can be failed and peers done while SIFT keeps runPromise pending; explicit resume and final partial export remain unavailable until settlement. Heartbeats continue without useful progress.

limits: Free pages alone are not total reclaimable RAM. Host observations support memory pressure, not a unique cause.
deviceMemory is an approximate physical-memory class, not current free memory or the Chromium ArrayBuffer pool ceiling.
Retired ownership bytes and policy credits do not prove browser GC completion.
No heap dump, debugger, browser allocation probe or OS OOM evidence identifies an exact allocator ceiling.
memoryEvidence.plannedSizeQualification: Derived plan bounds, not proven native failed extents; wrapper includes output, row, readInto and copies.

secondaryFinding.title: Released registry handle can retain identity strongly
secondaryFinding.reason: The tested raw ArrayBuffer identity remains reachable through release closure, but the production identity caller supplies SIFT worker record rec and clears its worker on retirement. Tested segmented regular/adopted SAB banks do become collectable after spill.

proposedDesign: Single exact allocation contract: domain, requested bytes, operation, generation, native cause, rollback and ownership; reject bounds errors as programming errors rather than memory pressure.

Recovery arbiter per allocation domain: grant one useful continuation and its dependency chain; pressure delays competing new growth but cannot block every repairing continuation. Unrelated admitted CPU/GPU work remains runnable.

One dependency model for every wait. Detect closed waiting components with no genuine CPU/GPU/IO producer and choose a continuation or settle as blocked with retained checkpoints. Do not use short fixed timeouts to kill productive work.

Reusable exact-size or size-class buffers and readInto destinations; include transfer/map/spill peaks in admission. Retire aliases only after acknowledgements. Avoid allocating a large copy in order to evacuate memory.

Adapt in-flight allocation width and eligible tile sizes from useful work, without preflight probes, quality reduction, persistent history or permanent global worker reduction. Preserve halo, arithmetic and ordering when splitting.
Transactional per-tile texture mask with committed bitmap; retain completed descriptor/field products. Add safe iteration/front checkpoints only with scientific parity and measured whole-run cost.

Unified failure/reclaim/wait/resume/publication events and automatic partial settlement when no useful producer can resolve a stall. Keep five comparable actual failures without own useful progress; track structural deadlock separately.
requiredRegressions: Two and many simultaneous failures in one domain; third producer present then gone; at least one retry progresses without cycle or pressure leak.
Native allocation and storage bounds errors through RGB/SIFT/Elastic preserve exact distinct cause, domain and requested extent.
Backend credits released in another domain, delayed retirement, shared buffers pinned by peers, incomplete IO and nested reclaim do not create false retry evidence or deadlock.
Mid-texture failure retains committed tile bitmap and output, retries only unfinished work, exact final scientific results and RNG state.
One detector terminal plus another structurally stuck yields explicit resumable partial state without replaying completed groups.
Full cold 96 MP after targeted proofs, total wall time includes useful computation, migration, recovery, export and verification; success only verified final archive.
whyPriorTestsMissedIt: Pressure admission tests cover one recovering owner and children; graph cycle tests exercise a separate registry wait path. Their composition with concurrent SiftPool retry re-admission was not covered. RGB error wrapping was not tested end-to-end with allocator recovery, and the smaller successful fixture did not hit the same refusal conditions.

externalSources.supports: deviceMemory is rounded approximate physical memory with implementation-defined bounds, not current allocatable memory.
Chromium uses a distinct ArrayBuffer partition and configurable pool when the V8 cage is enabled. This does not identify the exact ceiling of the tested Chrome build.
